City of Cabot

The Cabot City Council held its monthly Agenda Meeting on Tuesday, January 2, 2018 in the City Annex
Council Chambers. Council members present were: Ed Long, Rick Prentice, Kevin Davis, Damon Bivins, Ann
Gilliam, Ronald Waymack and Doug Warner. Norma Naquin was absent. Others present: Mayor Cypert,
City Attorney Jim Taylor, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Ed Long, Chairman of the Public Works Committee called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

Public Works:
1. Senior Center Kitchen & Dining Facilities Update — No Action — Legislation will be available at the
Council Meeting for discussion.
2. Public Works Community Input - None

Budget & Personnel: (Ann Gilliam)
1. Appoint Chad Young to the Planning Commission — Mayor recommends this appointment and
requests the second and third reading be suspended and voted on at the first reading. Motion by
Ed to include this item in this month’s council meeting agenda, second by Damon. Motion passed
with a vote of 7-0.
2. Budget & Personnel Community Input — None

Police & Fire: (Rick Prentice)
1. Monthly Report — Fire Department — None
2. Police Report — Police had a successful year of C.O.P. S. Toy Patrol with 55 kids shopping with
officers.
3. Central Fire Station / Farmer’s Market / Walking Trail — Discussion only — No action. See attached
for all documents distributed by the Mayor and his talking points. Points discussed:
a. Land price not included in pricing
b. Size of the two farmers market buildings being 35x80 each
c. Renovating Lowman’s building as a farmers market to revitalize downtown area & give
back to a pillar of the community
d. Timing of information being sent to council
e. Use of the farmers market buildings as other
f. Management of farmers market buildings
g. The title of Farmers Market for the buildings vs Outdoor Event Center or other
h. Location parking
i. Walking track size being less than .25 miles
Jj. Location lighting
k. Price increasing or not the next 30 days
Ron, Ann, Ed, and Kevin all voiced interest in discussing at a later date and not voting on this at
this time.
4. Police & Fire Community Input — None

Community Development: (Kevin Davis)
1. Community Development — Kevin Davis stated the online survey by Boyette is complete and the
information should have been emailed to you. A plan will be made based on the results of this
survey.

New Central Fire Station 01-02-2018

We have been planning for a new Central Station for over two years on
property purchased by the City from Renew Church at the Corner of Richie
Road and SH 367 or South 2" Street. In the process, consideration was
given to constructing on the site a farmer's market and outside event venue
as well as a lighted walking trail. That obviously had to be in concert with
Renew Church for a perpetual joint use agreement for their parking facilities,
which are now being expanded and improved. We have negotiated that
agreement; and, the final draft is included in this packet.

We are recommending that we proceed with procuring funding bonded by
franchise taxes, bidding, and the construction of the complex. This project
will enhance a vibrant downtown area, be a catalyst for redevelopment along
South 2" Street, provide an outdoor venue setting and walking trail for the
neighboring residences as well as use by other citizens and compliment the
planned reinvestments in the Richie Road park by the Parks and Recreation
Commission. Those include special needs facilities, ball fields, and long term
a splash pad. The Farmer's Market operated by Cabot City Beautiful is a
positive event for the city; and, we encourage Cabot City Beautiful to
continue to enhance and expand this event concurrent with its original intent.
We have provided preliminary information for the last year or so with regard
to design,. projected cost, and potential financing. We have asked our RFQ'd
bond underwriter, Stephens Inc., and bond counsel, Williams and Anderson,
to prepare funding cost estimates based on current interest which hopefully
will be reasonable. We have also asked our RFQ’d architect, Clements and
Associates, to proceed with bidding the project to compare with projected
costs. No formal action is proposed this evening other than notice that we

have fairly accurate construction costs.

Council Meeting Minutes
January 16, 2018

Call to Order
Mayor Bill Cypert called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City Council at
7:00 p.m. on January 16, 2018 in the Cabot City Annex Council Chambers.
Opening prayer was given by Council Member Ann Gilliam, and the Pledge of
Allegiance was led by Ed Long.

CITY COUNCIL MEETING 01-16-2018

Upon the recommendation of our Human Resources Director, Matthew Hood, we implemented
an Employee of the Month program in 2013. It has been very successful as an incentive for
employees, good public relations with citizens through press releases of the activity monthly,
and helps employees better connect with the Mayor and Human Resources Director by taking
the Employee of the Month to Lunch.

Employees of the Month are nominated by their peers. Over the past five years, the City has
recognized employees who have went above and beyond as the employee of the month. While
being a supervisor does not disqualify an individual from receiving the honor, the City tends to
choose employees who are not Department Heads.

We are pleased to announce the Animal Services Director, Mike Wheeler, is recognized as
January Employee of the Month for his hard work and dedication.

During these five years though, Animal Services Director Mike Wheeler has been nominated
multiple times from various Departments. Even though he has been extremely deserving, the
City has chosen someone else as Mike is an extremely modest individual who gives all the credit
to his employees and volunteers. He has even specifically stated he does not wish to win the
award. Lately though, some of Mike’s accomplishments are too great to ignore.

Each year the City of Cabot has some of the lowest euthanasia rates in the state, if not the
country. Since Mike has taken over, that rate has dropped dramatically. Recently Mike informed
the administration that at the end of December, the City of Cabot is at 1.8%, down from 35.3%
in 2009, the year he was employed, which means a live release rate of 98.2%. Nearly 3,700
animals left the shelter alive.

Recently Mike applied for and received a grant for $20,000 to help lower adoption fees on older
dogs and cats. This will help with adoption for some of the older animals which tend to be harder
to find homes for.

The Animal Shelter constantly brings pride to the City of Cabot. Whether it’s the numerous
Saturday events, adopting out pets to local and even out of state citizens, providing low cost
shots or microchips; something positive is always happening. Mike is at the forefront of this. He
is sometimes asked by Mayors of other cities, animal groups, and professional groups for
information and support based on his knowledge and operation of the Cabot Animal Services.
His dedication and love for the City, and most importantly, the animals, make him an easy choice
for employee of the month.

For being chosen employee of the month, Mike will receive a plaque with his name on it, his
name added to the list of employees chosen as employee of the month on the City Hall plaque,
his story in the newspaper, and lunch with the Mayor and the Human Resources Director.

The City will choose an employee each month based on their hard work from the month before.

Rick Prentice asked the council if all were aware of the changes made to the Central Fire Station plan. Rick
announced the walking track with lighting and the Farmers Market pavilions with restrooms had been
removed from the plans and they would discuss just the Central Fire Station only tonight. Rick also stated
he would like to see an agreement on the plans passed on to the full council meeting for adoption and
not have to have the Special Council Meeting already scheduled for Thursday night, February 15th.
Discussion. Norma stated she was ok with the Fire Station only but nothing else and her reason for not
wanting the walking track was due to the close proximity to the existing walking track/park on Richie Road.

--- page 3 (OCR) ---
Discussion. Mayor Cypert addressed the council with property acquisition, background, current status and
final strategy information. Please see attached for his talking points. Discussion. Mayor Cypert asked that
the full walking track be considered given the City requirements for sidewalks already make up seventy-
two percent of the walking track in the plan. Sharon Prentice asked about the need for an emergency
signal seeing none in the plans. Discussion. Chief Robinson stated it would be a benefit but not a necessity
since the truck will be in full view with lights flashing and sirens on as it pulls out of the station making its
way to Second Street. Mayor Cypert stated this project could be bid out with a seven percent contingency
plan to possibly finance an emergency signal if needed. Discussion. Some members of the Council stated
they agreed with this assessment since it was coming from the Fire Chief as the expert. When asked by
Rick for Citizen’s input, one citizen voiced his opposition to building a walking track stating the money
could be used for other essential things. Discussion. Travis Young, Executive Director of Cabot Parks and
Rec, stated they have put a substantial investment into the existing park on Richie Road but would like to
walk hand in hand with the City and are waiting for guidance. Chief Robinson asked the council to consider
the walking track as a means for the firefighters to stay fit and in compliance with the Departments fitness
requirements. Battalion Chief Cimino also asked the council to consider the walking track. He stated it
would be greatly used and pointed out multiple firefighters can use the track at the same time vs only one
on the indoor equipment. He also pointed out the use of the park on Richie Road by firefighters brought
an element of concern for the children and people that are enjoying the park if they were to have to leave
quickly in an emergency. Discussion. City Attorney Jimmy Taylor advised the council to make a motion
regarding the plans and a separate motion to send to full council. Motion by Norma to approve the plans
for the fire station only with a seven percent contingency, no waivers on the sidewalks, and sidewalks by
the UDC guidelines, (no lighting, no pavilions, and no outdoor bathrooms), second by Kevin. Motion
passed with a vote of 7-0. (Ann Gilliam had previously left the meeting). Motion by Kevin to place this
item on the agenda for this month’s council meeting, second by Damon. Motion passed with a vote of 7-
0.

Cabot’s bond counsel and Jack Truemper, Senior Vice President, Stephens, Inc.
also were in attendance.

stating cighty-nine percent of the bonds were sold to individuals with a true interest cost
of three point seven eight percent. An overall good success. Mr. Truemper also
announced the City has two redemption provisions. One — if there are un-expendable
proceeds, they can be returned; and two ~ after five years, the bonds can be redeemed in
part or in full in inverse order should the City be able to pay them off or refinance them
with a lower interest rate.

A RESOLUTION APPROVING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN OUTDATED
DOCUMENTS OF THE CABOT POLICE DEPARTMENT; AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES
WHEREAS, the Police Department for the City of Cabot, has accumulated a large
amount of outdated records and materials; and
WHEREAS, due to the lack of storage space, it has become necessary to destroy these
documents to allow current data adequate space to be stored; and
WHEREAS, Arkansas Code Annotated §14-59-114 allows for the destruction of said
records if supported by an affidavit signed by the municipal employee performing the destruction
and one (1) council member.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1:
Pursuant to Arkansas Code Annotated §14-59-114, the supporting
affidavit signed by Jackie Davis Chief of Police and Ann Gilliam, City Council Member, the
City Council does hereby authorize the destruction of various documents as set forth in the
affidavit attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by this reference.
SECTION 2: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after the date of
its passage.

AFFIDAVIT
A request is hereby made to the City Council for permission to destroy (recycle via compactor
and/or shredder) outdated records and materials of the Cabot Police Department. Due to lack of
storage space, it has become necessary to destroy these documents and allow current data
adequate space to be stored.
Per statute Arkansas Code Annotated § 14-2-204, case files and support documents are to be
maintained for a period of at least seven (7) years; therefore the Chief of Police requests that
the following support documents dated prior to January 1, 2010 be destroyed:

permanently maintained and will comply with Arkansas Code Annotated §§ 12-12-104 and 14-2203(b)(1) and that the records related to crimes of violence as defined by Arkansas Code
Annotated § 5-42-203 will be kept permanently. All documents previously mentioned for
destruction are included in the auditing process. Since the City of Cabot is audited annually, the
documentation has already been part of prior audits.

Cabot City Council Agenda Meeting
Cabot City Annex / Council Chambers
March 5, 2018
6:30 p.m.

The Cabot City Council held its monthly Agenda Meeting on Monday, March 5, 2018 in the City Annex
Council Chambers. Council members present were: Ed Long, Rick Prentice, Kevin Davis, Damon Bivins, Ann
Gilliam, Ronald Waymack, Doug Warner and Norma Naquin. Others present: Mayor Cypert, City Attorney
Jim Taylor, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Ed Long, Chairman of the Public Works Committee, called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

Public Works:

1. Parks and Recreation Commission Report — Ken Kincade, Chairman of the Recreation Commission,
presented the annual Parks and Rec report. A copy is attached to these minutes. Travis Young.
Cabot Parks and Recreation General Director distributed a 3 Year Capital/Project List. A copy is
attached to these minutes.

2. Animal Services Report — Mike Wheeler, Animal Services Director, presented their annual report.
A copy of the report is attached to these minutes.

3. Public Works Community Input — None

Budget & Personnel: (Ann Gilliam)

1. Destroy outdated police records — Chief Davis requested this legislation be voted on at the March
Council Meeting as routine records retention allowable by state law. Motion to place this item
on this month’s Council Meeting agenda by Doug, second by Norma. All voted yes.

2. Budget & Personnel Community Input — None

Police & Fire: (Rick Prentice)
1. Monthly Report — Fire Department — None
2. Monthly Report - Police Report — None
3. Police & Fire Community Input — None

Community Development: (Kevin Davis)
1. Community Development — Kevin Davis announced there will be a steering committee meeting
on March 28" at noon.
2. Community Development Community Input — Naomi Bratton addressed the council with an
update on HELP (Housing, Education, and Life Skills Program) to benefit the homeless community.
Memberships have increased, the Board is in place, and they are in the process of filing for a 501

(c) (3).

General Community input — Nick Whitaker asked why the City did not give the monetary donation
received for a Cabot PD K-9 to Lonoke County for their use. It was explained by Mayor Cypert the City has
plans to utilize the funds for a City K-9 in 2019.

REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS (RFQ)
The City of Cabot, Arkansas requires the services of a qualified consultant to provide engineering
services for the implementation of an interconnected and automated state-of-the-art coordinated
signal system for the City of Cabot. The work will generally consist of the development of a (1)
system engineering analysis, (2) environmental documents (3) signal design and communication
plans, (4) procurement documents, and (5) construction and implementation inspection - Title II
Services. Submittals must be received by 4:00 p.m. CST, May 8, 2018. To obtain a copy of the
RFQ and Notice of Nondiscrimination please contact Crystal Callahan at 501 605 0554 (hearing
impaired may dial 711).

REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS AND PROPOSALS
FOR ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES 04/02/2018
CITY OF CABOT SIGNAL NETWORK

A. PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The City of Cabot intends to modernize the City's Traffic Signal Network through improved
communications, signal interconnectivity, and use of a system network system for traffic
monitoring and signal functions. The consultants work is expected to consist of the development
of a (1) system engineering analysis, (2) environmental documents, (3) signal design and
communication plans, (4) procurement documents, (5) construction inspection and
implementation - Title II Services and other items necessary for the implementation of the signal
system.
B. SCOPE OF WORK
The following services will be provided by the consultant.
System Engineering Analysis
A system engineering analysis is required for the signal network.

The systems

engineering analysis must identify (1) operational goals of the corridor(s) by corridor (through
coordination with the local agency(s), (2) system requirements, (3) and system performance
evaluation measures.
The systems engineering analysis reports shall address the following federal requirements
contained in 23 CFR 940.11
1. Identification of portions of the regional ITS architecture being implemented
2. Identification of participating agencies roles and responsibilities
3. Requirements definitions
4. Analysis of alternative system configurations and technology options to meet

requirements
5. Procurement options
6. Identification of applicable ITS standards and testing procedures
7. Procedures and resources necessary for operations and management of the system

113

The systems engineering analysis shall be in a tabular format as detailed in the FHWA Model
Systems Engineering Documents.

Environmental Documentation
Prepare an environmental clearance document. The project will consist of data collect and
assessment of project's impact on social, economic, and natural environments. The consultant
will document these impacts in a Categorical Exclusion.

Sec. 4-114. - Pit Bull dogs.

(a) General. It shall be unlawful to keep, harbor, own, allow to run at large, or in any way possess a Pit
Bull dog within the corporate city limits, with the following exceptions: while transporting the dog
through the corporate city limits and while transporting to a veterinarian office (restrained and
muzzled) within the corporate city limits, unless the Pit Bull dog was properly registered with the city
prior to August 20, 2007. Properly registered Pit Bull dogs may be kept within the city provided said
dog shall be properly confined indoors or in a securely enclosed and locked pen as set forth in this
section Code.
(b) Leash. No person shall permit a registered Pit Bull to go outside its kennel or pen unless such dog is
securely leashed with a leash no longer than four feet in length. No person shall permit Pit Bull dogs
to be kept on a chain, rope or other type of leash outside its kennel or pen unless a person is in
physical control of the leash. Such dogs may not be leashed to inanimate objects such as trees,
posts, buildings, etc.
(c) Confinement outdoors. All registered Pit Bull dogs shall be securely confined indoors or in a securely
enclosed and locked pen or kennel, except when leashed as above provided. Such pen, kennel, or
structure must have secure sides and a secure top attached to the sides. All structures used to
confine registered Pit Bull dogs must have a secure bottom or floor attached to the sides of the pen
or the sides of the pen must be embedded in the ground. All structures erected to house Pit Bull
dogs must comply with all zoning and building regulations of the city. All such structures must be
adequately lighted and ventilated and kept in a clean and sanitary condition.
(d) Confinement indoors. No Pit Bull dog may be kept on a porch, patio or in any part of a house or
structure that would allow the dog to exit such building on its own volition. In addition, no such animal
may be kept in a house or structure when the windows are open or when screen windows or screen
doors are the only obstacle preventing the dog from exiting the structure.
(e) Signs. All owners, keepers or harborers of registered Pit Bull dogs within the city shall display a sign
in a prominent place on their premises. A sign is also required to be posted on the kennel or pen of
such animal.
(f)

Identification. All owners, keepers or harborers of registered Pit Bull dogs must provide annual color
photographs of the registered animal clearly showing the color and approximate size.

(g) Reporting requirements. All owners, keepers or harborers of registered Pit Bull dogs must report the
following information in writing to city animal services within ten days of the incident:
(1) The removal from the city or death of a registered Pit Bull dog.
(2) The birth of offspring of a registered Pit Bull dog.
(3) The new address of a registered Pit Bull dog owner should the owner move within the corporate
city limits.
(h) Sale or transfer of ownership prohibited. No person shall sell, barter or in any other way dispose of a
Pit Bull dog registered with the city to any person within the corporate city limits unless the recipient
resides permanently in the same household and on the same premises as the registered owner of
such dog; provided that the registered owner of the Pit Bull dog may sell or otherwise dispose of a
registered dog or offspring of such dog to persons who do not reside within the corporate city limits.
(i)

Animals born of registered dogs. All offspring born of Pit Bulls registered with the city must be
removed from the city within six weeks of the birth of such animal.

(j)

Irrefutable presumptions. There shall be an irrefutable presumption that any dog registered with the
city as a Pit Bull dog is subject to the requirements of this section.

(k) Procedures for dealing with registered and non-registered violators. Owners, keepers or harborers of
any dog found to be in violation of city law shall be guilty of a violation and be subject to punishment
as provided for pursuant to the following:

(1) The animal will be seized by city animal services and held for three business days for the owner
to reclaim the dog with a Pit Bull reclaim fee.
(2) The owner must sign an affidavit agreeing to immediately move the animal out of the corporate
city limits.
(3) The animal must be spayed or neutered at the owner's expense prior to its release to the
owner.
(4) Animals not reclaimed within three business days as prescribed shall be humanely destroyed by
city animal services personnel or sent to a suitable rescue outside of the corporate city limits.
(5) Any person violating or permitting the violation of any provision of this section shall be subject to
fines and/or imprisonment set forth in the penalties section. Second offender convictions shall
include seizure of the animal by city animal services personnel to be humanely destroyed or
sent to a suitable rescue outside of the corporate city limits.

ORDINANCE NO. __ of 2018
AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE LEVY OF AN ADDITIONAL TWENTY
DOLLARS ($20.00) FINE TO HELP DEFRAY THE EXPENSE OF
INCARCERATING CITY PRISONERS PURSUANT TO A.C.A. § 16-17-129;
DECLARING AN EMERGENCY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
WHEREAS, the Arkansas General Assembly passed Act 209 of 2009, amending
A.C.A. § 16-17-129, which authorizes the city, by ordinance, to levy up to an additional
Twenty dollar ($20.00) fine, and not to exceed Twenty Dollars ($20.00), to help defray
the expense of incarcerating city prisoners; and
WHEREAS, it is in the best interest and welfare of the citizens of Cabot,
Arkansas, that an additional fine of Twenty Dollars ($20.00) be levied and collected from
each defendant who pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, is found guilty of, or forfeits
bond in all cases in the Cabot District Court within Cabot, Arkansas.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED, BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS:
SECTION 1: That pursuant to A.C.A. § 16-17-129 an additional fine of Twenty
Dollars ($20.00) shall be levied and collected from each defendant who pleads guilty or
nolo contendere to, is found guilty of, or forfeits bond in any case in the Cabot District
Court within Cabot, Arkansas.
SECTION 2: That the additional fine levied by the city under this Ordinance
shall be deposited into a special fund within the City Treasury, and the revenues
generated by the additional fine shall be used exclusively to help defray the cost of
incarcerating city prisoners.
SECTION 3: The additional fine authorized by this Ordinance shall apply to all
cases before the Cabot District Court, to include each charge, count, violation, or offense
that a defendant pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, is found guilty of, or forfeits bond
for, including each misdemeanor or traffic violation.

SECTION 4: The various provisions and parts of this Ordinance are hereby
declared to be severable, and, if any section or part of a section, or any provision or part
of a provision herein, is declared to be unconstitutional, inappropriate, or invalid by any
court of competent jurisdiction, such holding shall not invalidate or affect the remainder
of this Ordinance and to that extend the provisions hereto are declared to be severable.
SECTION 5: That all Ordinances or parts of Ordinances found to be in conflict
herewith, are hereby repealed.
SECTION 6:

Emergency Clause. Whereas, the collection of an additional

twenty dollars ($20.00) fine to help defray the expense of incarcerating city prisoners is
essential for the health and welfare of the City of Cabot, an emergency is hereby declared
and this Ordinance shall be effective immediately from and after the passage and any
publication as required by law.

TAP GRANT FOR CENTRAL ELEMENTARY
We recently applied for a TAP Grant to Build SRTS sidewalks all around Central Elementary School:

o Of the nine elementary schools in the Cabot area, Central Elementary is estimated as
the second top number of students that walk to school.

o Not only will this project enhance the safe walkability of elementary school students, but
of all residents in the area.

o Pond Street being the primary automobile access to Central Elementary is very busy
and congested during the two peak traffic periods for the school, morning and
afternoon. The mixture of automobiles and students walking in the street, crossing, or
nearby is a dangerous mixture for serious accidents.

o This project is needed for the long-term viability and revitalization of the area.

We were not successful in obtaining the submitted grant; although, we felt like we had a good case. In
any event will continue applying for smaller grants and construct in phases which are easier to obtain
grants for:

o Ivanhoe west to Kerr Station
o lvanhoe east to Pine Street
o Connection streets from the north

This grant is for Phase | Ivanhoe west to Kerr Station.
Grant amount of $50,000 with a required $12,500 match, total project estimated at $69,750.

The Schoo! District is partnering with us in that the City will construct the sidewalk on easement in front
of Central Elementary and they are planning to expand the parking at Cabot Middle School South and
will build and pay for stacking lanes off street of Panther Trail, basically an equal partnership in the
amount of funding required for both.

We recently completed a sidewalk on Ivanhoe south to Robin Lane which made SRTS walkability and
connectivity to most of Robinwood available.

| will also use this discussion to point out that the City and School District are partnering 60/40 % in
installing a pedestrian signal at Panther Trail to protect students and walkers for left and right turn traffic
from Pine Street, Quotes were solicited and contracted cost came in at $12,483 with installation to
begin shortly.

P & R NORTH CABOT INTERCHANGE LIGHTING

In early 2017 the City took advantage of an offer to sell shale from the North Lonoke County Regional
Park for use in constructing the North Cabot Interchange

The material has been excavated to the north of the BMX track and Police Shooting Range and is still
in progress scheduled to be complete late this year.

It was spoken to in the 03/20/2017 City Council Meeting regarding a contract with the buyer that “P &
R was OK with the removal with the request that the revenue be used for P & R projects” and is recorded
in the minutes. My intent was the Regional park.

It was further made clear in that meeting that the “ear marking of the revenue will be decided at a later
date by the City Council” again recorded in the minutes. The funding is now in the City General Fund.

Given that sidewalks and lighting are critical for the Interchange to avoid the long-term mistake of not
having at Exit 19, we intended to use the remaining bond funding for that project plus a $100,000 from
Lonoke County Judge Erwin.

The interchange cost itself has grown from a projected $19,000,000 to $26,000,000 plus to be covered

proceeds, they can be returned; and two - after five years, the bonds can be redeemed in
part or in full in inverse order should the City be able to pay them off or refinance them
with a lower interest rate.

PLAN; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, the Cabot Planning Commission is empowered to regulate and control the
development of land within the planning jurisdiction of the City of Cabot pursuant to Ark. Code Ann.
§14-56-417; and
WHEREAS, the Cabot Planning Commission held its regularly scheduled meeting on January
23rd, 2018 and approved the request of Bond Consulting Engineers, authorized agent for Helen Pruett
Trust, to rezone the real property located at 2170 W Main Street from
R-1, Single-Family
Residential, to C-2, General Commercial District, more specifically set forth in the legal description
attached hereto as Exhibit "A" and incorporated herein by this reference and referring the same to
this governing body for approval; and
WHEREAS, the Cabot Planning Commission further approved an amendment to the City's
Land Use Plan to reflect consistency with the change in use; referring the same to this body for
approval.
NOW THEREFORE HE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1: The property located at 21 70 W Main Street more specifically set forth in the
legal description attached hereto as Exhibit "A" and incorporated herein by this reference and on file
in the City Clerk-Treasurer's Office is hereby rezoned from R-1 to C-2.
SECTION 2: The City's Land Use Plan is hereby amended to incorporate the change in the
land use as stated above.
SECTION 3: Emergency. The proper and appropriate planning of the City is of great
importance to the health and welfare of its citizens, therefore an emergency is declared and this
Ordinance being necessary for the preservation of the public peace, health, safety and welfare shall
be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

SECTION 4.10 OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING REQUIREMENTS
4.10.1 Off-Street Parking and Loading Requirements
a. Applicability: Off-street parking and loading areas shall be required for all uses in all zoning
districts (excluding C-1: Central Business District). Off-street parking and loading areas shall
be required to meet the standards of this Section when:
i.

A building or structure is built or erected;

ii.

A building or structure is expanded or enlarged;

iii. An off-street parking or loading area is expanded;
iv. A use is established;
v.

A certificate of occupancy is requested;

vi. A nonconforming use or structure is otherwise required to come into compliance with the
provisions of this Zoning Code. See Section 4.11 regarding nonconformities.
Once established, required off-street parking and loading areas shall meet all the
requirements of this Section and shall not be diminished in number or reduced in size below
the requirements for its attached use. Such off-street parking and loading areas shall be
located on the same property or lot as its attached use or structure, unless subject to an
allowed shared parking agreement.
A required parking space may not be substituted for a loading space. A required loading
space may not be substituted for a parking space.
b. Establishment of Parking: Off-street parking and loading areas shall considered to be
established when paved and marked for use or when used on a permanent basis. A
permanent basis shall be considered once (1) per seven (7) days for a period of at least
thirty (30) days or as evidenced by signs of consistent use for parking by creation of barren
spot on the ground or presence of a graveled surface. Parking areas not considered
permanent shall not be subject to the requirements of this Section.
c. Site Plan Review: All parking improvements shall be reviewed through the Site Plan Review
process detailed in Section 4.8. Single-Family Dwellings, Two-Family Dwellings, and ZeroLot Line Dwellings are exempted from this requirement unless Site Plan Review is otherwise
required.
d. Number of Off-Street Parking Spaces Required: Where a fractional space results, any
fraction more than one-half (1/2) shall be counted as one (1) parking space. Where net floor
area is used, it shall mean building floor area less areas used for storage, utilities, or
building service. If a floor plan for the use is not available, 80% of gross floor area of the
structure shall be considered the net floor area.

4.10.2 Off-Street Loading Areas
a. Size: Each loading space shall be not less than 10 feet in width, 35 feet in length, and 14
feet in height. Where the off-street loading space does not abut on a street, alley, or
easement of access, there shall be provided an access drive of at least 10 feet in width
leading from the street to loading area.
b. Location: Such space may occupy all or any part of any required yard or court space, but
no such space may be located closer than 25 feet to any Residential District unless wholly
within a completely enclosed building or unless enclosed on all sides abutting the
Residential District by a wall or solid fence at least eight (8) feet in height.
4.10.3 Shared Parking Agreements
The following shall govern the allowance of shared parking agreements:
a. In instances where a mix of uses create staggered peak parking demand periods, shared
parking agreements may be used to meet parking requirements. No shared parking
agreement shall be used for this purpose when including parking for residential uses.
b. Shared parking agreements shall be reviewed by the Administrative Official at the time of
Site Plan Review. If a site plan is not otherwise required, the agreement shall be reviewed at
the time of building permit or certificate of occupancy issuance. The Administrative Official
shall review such agreement to determine its compliance with the standard of this Code.
Such agreements shall be created to apply to successive owners/occupants in perpetuity as
long as the use to which the agreement is tied continues.
c.

Shared parking agreements may not be used to meet greater than thirty (30) percent of the
parking requirement and shall not be used to meet required loading and unloading areas or
spaces.

d. Shared parking shall meet the following standards:
i.

Shared parking shall accessible by car as well as by sidewalk and be located within 300
feet of the building or use with which its intended to be shared.

ii.

Shared parking shall not require crossing a street for access.

iii. Shared parking shall be guaranteed by an executed legally binding agreement between
the owner of parking area and the owner of the building or use served by the parking
area. Such agreement shall provide for the continuing provision of parking for the
lifespan of the use or building regardless of owner, successor, or heir.

3-9-222. Private clubs -- Procedure for obtaining permit.
(a)
(1) Application for a permit to operate as a private club may be made to the governing body of the county or
municipality in which the private club seeks to be located.
(2) If the governing body of the county or municipality approves by ordinance an application for a permit to
operate as a private club under subdivision (a)(1) of this section, the Alcoholic Beverage Control
Division may issue a permit to operate as a private club to the applicant for the proposed location.
(b)
(1) The application for a private club shall be submitted to the division and accompanied by an annual
permit fee of one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500).
(2) The application for a bed and breakfast private club shall be submitted to the division and accompanied
by an annual permit fee of seventy-five dollars ($75.00).
(3) In an area in which the sale of intoxicating liquor has not been authorized by local option as provided
under § 3-8-201 et seq., the application for a private club permit shall be submitted to the division and
accompanied by an additional application fee of one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500).
(c)
(1) After filing an acceptable application with the Director of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division, the
applicant shall cause to be published at least one (1) time each week for four (4) consecutive weeks in
a legal newspaper of general circulation in the city in which the premises are situated or, if the
premises are not in a city, in a newspaper of general circulation for the locality where the business is to
be conducted, a notice that the applicant has applied for a permit to dispense alcoholic beverages on
the premises.
(2) The notice shall be in such form as the director shall prescribe by rule or order and shall be verified.
(3) The notice shall give the names of the managing agent and the nonprofit corporation or, in the case of a
bed and breakfast private club, the name of the business owner, and shall state:
(A) That the manager, or in the case of a bed and breakfast private club, the owner, at least one (1)
partner, or the majority stockholder is a citizen of Arkansas;
(B) That he or she is of good moral character;
(C) That he or she has never been convicted of a felony or had a license to sell or dispense alcoholic
beverages revoked within the five (5) years preceding the date of the notice; and
(D) That he or she has never been convicted of violating the laws of this state or of any other state
governing the sale or dispensing of alcoholic beverages.
(d)

(1) Within five (5) days after filing an application for a permit to dispense alcoholic beverages on the
premises, a notice of the application shall be posted in a conspicuous place at the entrance to the

(2) The applicant shall notify the director of the date when the notice is first posted.
(3) No permit shall be issued to any applicant until proper notice has been so posted on the premises for at

(4)
(A) The notice shall be in such form as the director shall prescribe by rule or order.

(ii) Printed in black lettering on a yellow background.
(e)
(1) Upon receipt by the director of an application for a permit, written notice thereof, which shall include a
copy of the application, the application shall immediately be mailed by the director to the sheriff, chief
of police, if located within a city, prosecuting attorney of the locality in which the premises are situated,
and city board of directors or other governing body of the city in which the premises are situated if
within an incorporated area. The provisions of this section shall be retroactive to July 28, 1995.
(2) No license shall be issued by the director until at least thirty (30) days have passed from the mailing by
the director of the notices required by this section.
(3) Upon receipt by the director within the thirty (30) days of a protest against the issuance of a permit by a
governing official of the city or county to whom the notice of an application for permit has been mailed,
the director shall not issue the license until he or she has held a public hearing.
(f) Upon the director's determining that the applicant is qualified hereunder and that the application is in the
public interest, a permit may be issued as authorized in this section.

Council Meeting Minutes
April 16, 2018
Call to Order
Mayor Bill Cypert called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City Council at
7:00 p.m. on April 16, 2018 in the Cabot City Annex Council Chambers. Opening
prayer was given by Council Member Kevin Davis, and the Pledge of Allegiance
was led by Council Member Norma Naquin.
Mayor Cypert awarded Annika Franovich with a Hero Award.

Roll Call
A roll call was conducted. The following persons were present: Council Member,
Rick Prentice, Ronald Waymack, Doug Warner, Damon Bivins, Ed Long, Ann
Gilliam, Norma Naquin, and Kevin Davis. Also in attendance were Mayor Bill
Cypert, City Attorney Jimmy Taylor, and City Clerk / Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters
The minutes of the March Regular Council Meeting were approved with a motion by Mr.
Warner, and second by Mr. Waymack. All voted yes by a Roll Call vote.
The minutes of the February Special Council Meeting were approved with a motion by
Ms. Naquin, and second by Mr. Waymack. All voted yes by a Roll Call vote.
Motion to read legislation by title only by Ms. Gilliam second by Mr. Prentice. All voted
yes by a Roll Call vote.

Planning Commission

OTHER PURPOSES was read by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Third reading. Ms.
Naquin announced the ordinance title did match the legal description on ARCountyData.com.
Discussion. Motion by Mr. Davis to Table this ordinance until the May Council Meeting,
second by Mr. Prentice. Motion passed 8-0 by a Roll Call Vote.

repealed to the extent of the conflict and if conflicts between this Ordinance and other City

MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 20, 2018 AS PRESENTED, SECOND BY
JOHN C. THOMPSON. ALL VOTED AYE.

III.

Financials
March 2018 financials were discussed. Bidding process for the Richie Road project was
discussed. Parks and Recreation Director suggest a rebid on project, with the addition of special
addendums required for said project. Greg Crumpton suggests a motion to rebid the project.
MIKE BURCHFIELD MOTIONED TO AUTHORIZE A REQUEST FOR COMPREHENSIVE BID
PROCESS AND THE ADDITION OF THE NULLIFICATION FOR PARKS AND RECREATION DIRECTOR
TO RESUBMIT CUMULATIVE PROJECTS, SECOND BY ERIC PARK. NO DISCUSSION. VOTE
PASSES. MATT MOUDY MOTIONED TO NULLIFY AND RESUMBIT PREVIOUS BIDS AND TO
AUTHORIZE REBID, SECOND BY MIKE BURCHFIELD. ALL VOTED AYE. Questions pertaining to
contractual obligations and statutes regarding qualified bidding and applicants were discussed.

IV.

Programs
Business as usual. Rain has been an issue in recent weeks. Baseball, softball, and tennis
programs have all started. Parks Director discussed partnership with Leaping Beyond and
current registration status for the special needs baseball program, set to begin April 19, 2018.
Current enrollment status for Leaping Beyond baseball program is 28 kids. Adult basketball, flag
football, and volleyball registrations have begun.
Thomas Paulson presented for Flag football. Major weather hiccups have hurt the season.
Inclement weather occurred two weeks ago and complaints were made to Parks and Recreation
staff. Mr. Paulson indicated that with 42 teams, no cancellations or rescheduling of games
would occur during this Spring season. Mr. Paulson discussed that cancellations are not ideal
and due to unavailability of referees, games cannot be played during the week or on Sundays.

183

Commission and Parks Director questioned this statement, siting $1500 worth of repairs made
to school property on Flag Footballs behalf. Decisions to eradicate this issue were discussed. In
the event of inclement weather, Parks Director and/ or Programs Director will arrive at location
before scheduled games to determine playability and to accommodate for avoidable damages.
BMX presented. Weather has not been an issue. Races are during the week. Numbers continue
to increase. Two renewals and a new rider sign up in one week. State race is a big goal for the
future. Dirt will be moved in on 4/18 and 4/19. BMX will not shutdown during rebuild. Parks
Director discussed the clearing out and removing canopy of trees for track accessibility. New
parking for BMX discussed.
V.

Old Business
Old Business was discussed. Mayor inquiry about Parks Department cutting city grass was
discussed. Prices for service: $2500/cut, $44,000-$47,000 for everything. The City of Cabot
Mayor has determined that the City of Cabot will continue to service and cut areas.

VI.

New Business
Parks director discussed the need and requested for a CPR Engineer/ Architect to be placed on
a continuous contract. Need based on current and future Parks and Recreation projects. Parks
Director suggests that the RFQ process should be sent out and prices for contract should be
discussed. JOHN C. THOMPSON MOTIONED TO AUTHORIZE THE RFQ PROCESS, SECOND BY
MATT MOUDY. ALL VOTED AYE.

None

Minutes-The Commissioners reviewed the minutes for the March 2018 meeting. Motion to approve was made by Billy Johnson,
with Ann Gillam making the second. The commission voted, but Ed Long abstained because he was not here last month. Minutes
were approved.
Financial Report- The Commission reviewed the March 2018 financial report. Jay Lallu made a motion to approve the financial
report, with Ann Gillam making the second. The financial report for March was approved.
Funding Request- Caroline Bonifant and Jenny Ross were here from Master Gardner’s. They were asking for $2,500.00 to help
beautify Cabot. They will be placing shrubbery, flowers and trees around Cabot so that you will see it as you are entering into the
city. This will help to beautify our city. They also asked for an annual amount of $500 to be budgeted to them for upkeep of these
areas. A motion to approve was made by Ed Long with a 2nd by Ann Gillam. The motion was approved.
Chamber Report- Amy Williams went over the Chamber report by phone. She reported that we had 5 new members last month.
We have had lots of ribbons cuttings. There was also a big announcement for Cabot in that a hospital will be built here. It will be a
small hospital with 8-10 beds with room to grow. This is huge for Cabot.
Parks and Recreation Report- Travis Young reported that we have great numbers here for softball this year. We also had more
baseball teams in Cabot for tournaments in the month of March than we ever have. April has been slow, but we feel good about the
direction that we are going. On Thursday nights, we will be having baseball games for kids with special needs. We are working
now on getting turf put on one of the fields for this. We hope to have a special needs soccer program this fall with hopes at doing a
tennis program as well.
General Discussion- Tommy Hignight brought up the A&P tax collections and the fact that he feels that the Chamber should be in
charge of the whole process of collecting and everything. He has spoken to the mayor and Tammy Yokum, the city clerk/treasurer
and neither one of them have a problem with it. Tommy also has checked with other surrounding cities on how they do it and there
are different ways. Some do the same way Cabot does currently, with the city collecting the taxes, some have an outside firm doing
it and some have their Chamber of Commerce office do it. He made it known that it was in his opinion, he thinks that the Chamber
should do this. He said that they would formally talk about this in the May A&P meeting and for everyone to please give it some
thought before then.
Clint McGue, reported that we have seen good response from the letters sent about the delinquencies on A&P taxes. We have
received at least partial payment from most of those that letters were sent to. Cabot Café and Cake Corner has yet to pay any A&P
taxes and that their delinquency dates back to 2016. The last certified letter that we sent to them, was signed for, but we have yet to
be contacted. Clint asked if the commission wished to move forward in revoking their A&P tax permit and closing them down. A
motion was made by Jay Lallu to move forward with revoking the A&P license of Cabot Café & Cake Corner and a 2nd was made
by Ed Long. The commission voted and it was approved.
The next A&P meeting will be May 15, 2018 at 8:30am.
The motion to adjourn the meeting was made by Billy Johnson and 2nd made by Jay Lallu at 9:18 a.m.

Detective Ringgold went to the concession area and purchased two Michelob

Detective Koonce went to the concession area and purchased two Bud Light beers

The business also has conditions that alcoholic beverages cannot enter the
bathroom area and there are no sales after 10:00 p.m. Detective Koonce approached the
concession stand and purchased two tickets to Valerian at 9:45 p.m. Detectives Koonce

movie was being played.

Approximately 10:07 p.m., Detective Ringgold left the theater and approached the
concession stand and ordered a Michelob Ultra beer. Detective Ringgold paid $7.00 for
the beer and the employee marked the existing wristband. Detective Ringgold returned
back to the movie theater. Approximately 5 minutes later, Detectives Koonce and
Ringgold left the business.

BOARD DECISION

On the 16 day of March, 2016, the Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage Control
Board convened at Little Rock, Arkansas for its regular monthly meeting. In
attendance were Board Members Janet Moore, Chairperson, Mickey Powell,
Jean Hervey, Chris Palmer, Steve Smith and ABC Director Bud Roberts.

Mr. James Smith was present at the hearing and was represented by his
attorney, Steve Morley. Several members of the Little Rock Police Department
appeared in opposition to the request by James Smith to extend the hours in
which he may serve alcohol at the permitted premises and his request to do
away with the two drink per customer limit imposed by the ABC Board when
his application was granted on September 17, 2014.

After considering all sworn testimony and all material introduced into
evidence and contained in the application file, it is found:

REVIEW OF EVIDENCE OFFERED

1. Christopher Crane testified in support of Mr. Smith’s request, as follows:
that he represents the Arkansas Motion Picture Institute; that his institute has
film festivals at Riverdale from time to time; that the events might run from
11:00 in the morning to 11:00 p.m. at night; that some films that are shown at
Riverdale can only be seen there and that some people come from out of state in
order to see these films; and that he feels that it would promote the public

--- page 13 (OCR) ---
convenience and advantage to add to the existing hours of alcohol service at
Riverdale.

2. Matt Smith testified in support of his request, as follows: that his
patrons at Riverdale have approached him about expanding his hours of service
of alcoholic beverages; that some retired senior citizens want to come to an
earlier movie and it would be a convenience to them if they were able to
purchase alcoholic beverages at eleven o'clock; that some movies at film
festivals events do not start until 10:00 p.m.; that he has had no issues with
the ABC and has not had to call the Little Rock Police Department for any
problems; that he has held an ABC permit since 2007 and has had no
violations from the ABC; that émployces of Riverdale are able to observe the
patrons seated in the auditoriums because there are wide aisles that allow
employees to walk in between the rows in the theater auditoriums; that all
alcoholic beverages must be purchased from a central location in the theater
which is a well lit area; and that his employces will not sell any alcoholic
beverages to people that are intoxicated.

3. Detective Sergeant Alan Hamby of the Little Rock Police Department
testified that he is concerned that minors will be able to consume alcoholic
beverages inside the Riverdale Theatcr because it is not easy to observe and
monitor people that are consuming alcoholic beverages inside a movie theater.

Based upon the above testimony the Board, by a vote of 5-0, approves
Mr. Smith’s request to extend the hours of service of alcoholic beverages at
Riverdale from 11:00 a.m. until 11:00 p.m. That Board further votes to deny
Mr. Smith's request to do away with the two drink limit previously imposed on
him by the Board. The two drink per customer limit remains in effect,

DONE AT LITTLE ROCK, ARKANSAS, this 16% day of March, 2016.

A. PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The City of Cabot (City) intends to modernize the City's Traffic Signal Network through
improved communications, signal interconnectivity, and use of a network system for traffic
monitoring and signal functions. The consultant’s work is expected to consist of the development
of a (1) system engineering analysis, (2) environmental documents, (3) signal design and
communication plans, (4) procurement documents, (5) construction inspection and
implementation - Title II Services and other items necessary for the implementation of the signal

requirements

AN ORDINANCE ACCEPTING A PORTION OF HIGHWAY 367, SECTION 14,
BETWEEN HWY 321 AND HIGHWAY 38 INTO THE STREET SYSTEM FOR
THE CITY OF CABOT, LONOKE COUNTY, ARKANSAS FROM THE
ARKANSAS STATE HIGHWAY AND TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENT;
DELCARING AND EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, a portion of Highway 367, specifically Section 14, between Highway
321 and Highway 38 will be widening to five lanes upon completion of Job 061509 by
Arkansas Department of Transportation (ARDOT); and
WHEREAS, the City of Cabot desires to partner with ARDOT to expedite the
design and construction of said project; and
WHEREAS, the City of Cabot agrees to accept all ownership and full responsibility
for the maintenance of that portion of Highway 367, Section 14, between Highway 321
and Highway 38 with the roadway constructed by ARDOT Job 061509, in the City of
Cabot, which is to be transferred to the City of Cabot, in accordance with Arkansas Code
Annotated § 14-301-102; and
WHEREAS, acceptance of the proposed change and transfer is practical and will
be in the best interest of the City of Cabot and the public.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL FOR
THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS:
SECTION NO. 1:

The City of Cabot, Arkansas, hereby agrees and accepts

Highway 367, Section 14, between Highway 321 and Highway 38 with the roadway
constructed by ARDOT Job 061509, in the City of Cabot, into the City of Cabot’s City
Street System.
SECTION NO. 2:

Pursuant to Arkansas Code Annotated § 14-301-102, this

change to the State Highway System and the Cabot City Street System, reflected on
attached Exhibit "A", is hereby accepted and authorized by the City Council of the City of
Cabot, Arkansas.
SECTION NO. 3: A copy of the ordinance duly certified by the City Clerk shall
be filed in the office of the Recorder of Lonoke County and recorded in the deed of said

county.
SECTION NO. 4:

Upon completion of the roadway constructed by ARDOT

Job 061509, that portion of Highway 367, Section 14, between Highway 321 and
Highway 38, in the City of Cabot, Lonoke County and after the City of Cabot receives
official notification from the Deputy Director and Chief Engineer with ARDOT that said
portion of Highway 367 is removed from the State Highway System by the State
Highway Commission, this Ordinance shall take effect and be in force immediately
thereafter.
SECTION NO. 5: A copy of this Ordinance shall be submitted to the Arkansas
State Highway and Transportation Department for their records.
SECTION NO. 6: Emergency Clause. ARDOT will advance the bid letting date
to start construction of the Highway 321 widening from May 2020 to May 2019, 1 full year
earlier. The widening of that portion of Highway 367, Section 14, between Highway 321
and Highway 38, in the City of Cabot, is of proper and beneficial use for the City of Cabot,
Arkansas and is of great importance to the health and welfare of its citizens. An emergency
is therefore declared and this ordinance being necessary for the preservation of the public
peace, health, safety and welfare shall be in full force and effect.

AN ORDINANCE TO APPOINT LIZ BIRD TO THE CABOT PLANNING
COMMISSION; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, due to the resignation of, Jerrel Maxwell, the Cabot Planning Commission
currently has a vacancy; and
WHEREAS, the term of the vacant position expired July 9, 2018; and
WHEREAS, Liz Bird is a capable and qualified citizen of Cabot that desires to be
appointed to the Cabot Planning Commission; and
WHEREAS, Mayor Cypert hereby recommends the appointment of Liz Bird to fill the
vacant position of the expired term, subject to the approval of this governing body.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1: Liz Bird is hereby appointed to the Cabot Planning Commission.
SECTION 2: Liz Bird shall fill the vacant position on the Cabot Planning Commission
which expired July 9, 2018. Liz Bird’s term will begin immediately upon passage of this
ordinance and will expire July 9, 2023.
SECTION 3: EMERGENCY. The proper operation and appropriate planning of the
Planning Commission is of great importance to the health and welfare of the city of Cabot and its
citizens. An emergency is therefore declared and this Ordinance being necessary for the preservation
of the public peace, health, safety, and welfare shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

A RESOLUTION EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR APPLICATION TO THE
ARKANSAS DEPARTMENT OF PARKS AND TOURISM FOR ITS OUTDOOR
RECREATION GRANT PROGRAM; AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY
CLERK-TREASURER TO EXECUTE ANY NECESSARY DOCUMENTS AND TO
EXPEND FUNDS, IF NECESSARY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, Cabot, Arkansas seeks to improve the recreation facilities and wishes to seek
grant funding assistance; and
WHEREAS, in order to obtain the funds necessary to develop and/or improve the site for
such a recreation area, it is necessary to obtain a 50/50 Matching Grant from the Arkansas
Department of Parks and Tourism’s Outdoor Recreation Grant Program; and
WHEREAS, the plans for such recreation areas have been prepared and the price therefore
has been established; and
WHEREAS, this governing body understands the grantee and grantor will enter into a
binding agreement which obligates both parties to policies and procedures contained in the Land
and Water Conservation Fund Grants Manual including, but not limited to the following: the park
area defined by the project boundary map submitted in the application, must remain in outdoor
recreation use in perpetuity, regardless if the property is bought or developed with matching grant
funds and; all present and future overhead utility lines within the project boundary must be routed
away or placed underground and; the project area must remain open and available for use by the
public at all reasonable times of the day and year; facilities can be reserved for special events,
league play, etc. but cannot be reserved, leased or assigned for exclusive use, and; the project area
must be kept clean, maintained, and operated in a safe and healthful manner.
WHEREAS, the City Council is well aware and apprised of the above-mentioned project
and will provide the local portion of the development cost of the entire project.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1: The Mayor is hereby authorized to make application to the Arkansas
Department of Parks and Tourism for assistance with park improvements at Richie Road Park and
the Highway 321 Sports Plex for the City; therefore, such application shall be submitted as
expediently as possible.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE CITY COUNSEL OF THE CITY OF CABOT,

AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE CABOT FIRE
DEPARTMENT
TO
OPERATE
BEYOND
THE
CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, the citizens of the City of Cabot, Arkansas, have an interest in securing and
providing fire protection services to benefit those portions of Lonoke County that are underserved
or not served;
WHEREAS, the Cabot Fire Department wishes to provide fire protection services to
benefit those portions of Lonoke County that are underserved or not served;
WHEREAS, the Cabot Fire Department wishes to provide a method to collect costs of
providing services outside the city limits of the City of Cabot, Arkansas;
WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann. § 14-53-102 (the “Authorizing Legislation”) states in
pertinent part:
In order to prevent the destruction by fire of property located outside the corporate limits
of cities and towns and in order to lessen the loss caused on account of insufficient means
to combat fires and as a protection against such loss, the city council or other governing
body of any city or town having an organized fire department may provide by ordinance
that the firefighting machinery and equipment, with the necessary firefighters to operate it,
may be used to combat fires beyond the corporate limits of any city or town, upon such
terms, conditions, and restrictions as may be prescribed in the ordinance[;]
WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Cabot finds that there exists an immediate
need for fire protection services for portions of Lonoke County and desires to authorize the Cabot
Fire Department, to use the firefighting machinery and equipment, with the necessary firefighters
to operate it, along with all other reasonable actions necessary, to combat fires beyond the
corporate limits of the City of Cabot and within the borders of Lonoke County and to otherwise
comply with the requirements of the Authorizing Legislation by the adoption of this ordinance;
NOW THEREFORE, be it enacted by the City Council of the City of Cabot, Arkansas:
Article I:
Authorization. The Cabot Fire Department is hereby authorized, pursuant
to Ark. Code Ann. § 14-53-102, to use the firefighting machinery and equipment, with the
necessary firefighters to operate it, along with all other reasonable actions necessary, to combat
fires beyond the corporate limits of the City of Cabot, Arkansas. The Cabot Fire Department shall
have the right to refuse to respond to any request for service outside the corporate city limits if, in

the judgment of the fire chief, or authorized representative, the services within the city limits would
be impaired.
Article II:
Service Area. The Cabot Fire Department is authorized, but not required,
to operate in all unincorporated areas within the borders of Lonoke County.
Article III:

Payment.

A. Schedule of Payment
The person outside the city limits receiving the services of the city fire department as
contained herein shall, upon presentation of a bill for service, pay to the City of Cabot, Arkansas:
(1) An hourly charge equivalent to the regular hourly pay for each hour that each on-duty
employee of the department is involved in response, and the overtime rate or off-duty
rate of any off-duty employees who respond;
(2) Administrative costs plus employee benefit costs;
(3) Equipment depreciation costs;
(4) The replacement costs of all equipment damaged or made unusable by contamination;
in managing and mitigating the incident;
(5) Any costs incurred by the fire department with any labor, materials, or supplies
provided by a third party at the request of the fire department.
B. Mutual Aid, Automatic Aid, or Interlocal Agreements
If services are provided in accordance with a written mutual aid, automatic aid, or interlocal
agreement, charges, if any, will be issued as outlined in the applicable agreement.
Article IV: Severability. If any provision of this ordinance is held invalid, such invalidity
shall not affect other provisions of the ordinance which can be given effect without the invalid
provisions, and to this end the provisions of the ordinance are declared to be severable.
Article V: Repealer. All ordinances and resolutions, and parts thereof, which are in
conflict with any provision of this Ordinance are hereby repealed to the extent of such conflict.
Article VI: Emergency Clause. In order to provide fire protection for underserved
Lonoke County residents, to preserve the health, welfare, and safety of the underserved citizens of
the County, an immediate need exists for the adoption of this ordinance. Therefore, an emergency
is declared and this ordinance being necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace,
health, and safety shall be in full force and effect upon its enactment and approval.

SH 321 is one of the busiest urban two-lane highways in the state of Arkansas which should
have had capacity upgrades complete several years ago.

ARDOT has made plans to upgrade and has the funding: but, had been scheduled for a bid
letting in May 2020, which means construction would soon follow.

The long-term plan by the city and ARDOT was to partner to make it happen sooner and this
Ordinance is the result of those plans.

A precedence was set when the north UPRR overpass was built and accelerated by the city
and a partnership with the ARDOT taking over maintenance of SH 38 which then traversed
along Lincoln Street from SH 89 to the new overpass.

The entire stretch of US 367 through town has been overlayed and restriped with a long-
expected life cycle and is in excellent shape.

Capacity improvements from Main Street South are not expected to be needed until well into
the next decade if that; and, from Main Street North capacity improvements will be similar due
to the traffic reduction off SH367 by the North Cabot Interchange.

The five bridges on south SH 367 according to recent ARDOT bridge inspection reports are in
good shape and total maintenance costs since 2007 are an average of $3,896 annually, of
which a good part is guard rails that private insurance covered the cost of replacement from
vehicle accidents.

The ribbon cutting ceremony for the inclusive park off of Richie Road was successful. The

New Business
Cabot Youth Football Association (CYFA) is currently experiencing difficulties filling a secretarial
board position. Curtis and Kelly Rudd are present on behalf of CYFA. Parks Director Young
expressed the commissions roll in the approval of multiple family members active on a single
board. A spouse of an active board member has temporarily been filling the roll of CYFA
secretary. Officially, a spouse of an active board member may not fill the roll without Parks
Commission approval. Commissioner Cope indicated that the initial ruling was set in place to
avoid the unfair advantage of two voting members from a single family. Commissioner
Whitaker expressed to Curtis Rudd a previous experience with Travis Hudson. According to
Parks Commissioner Whitaker, Chris Easter was nominated to fill a position on the CYFA board,
but was advised not to by acting CYFA President Travis Hudson because of possible conflict of
interest, as Mr. Easter was currently serving as active member of the rules committee. Turning
down active volunteers in lieu of spouses creates the perception of a two vote stack.
Commissioner Whitaker inquired if Kelly Rudd had to be an active voting member in order to
fulfill the CYFA secretarial duties. Mrs. Rudd indicated that it would be an injustice to the
families who depend on the CYFA board if the answer was no. Posts regarding the position have
been made to Facebook, but the lack of volunteers during the CYFA off season creates an issue.
CYFA registrations will start in August and the season will begin in September. Commission
suggests advocating for the position during this time. Commissioner Sled suggests keeping the
position open temporarily, as the CYFA Constitution entitles the treasurer to fulfill the roll of
secretary until elected. Commission asks Parks Director Young if action needs to be taken. The
decision is left up to the Commission with the understanding of past agreements set forth by
CYFA and Commission Attorney Greg Crumpton. No motion.

WHEREAS, on June 13, 2012 the City and IESI Corporation, now Waste Connections,

the extent of the conflict.

if any section, phrase or provision shall be declared or held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect
the remainder of the sections, phrases, or provisions.

ARDOT PROPOSAL TO TAKE OVER MAINTENANCE ON SH 367 THROUGH TOWN
AND MOVE UP SH 321 CONSTRUCTION ONE YEAR

ARDOT made the proposal to the city some while ago. In a meeting earlier, this year the
Department asked if the City was willing to work with the Department to facilitate the
construction widening of SH 321 by assuming maintenance of SH 367 through town. We
indicated that we would. This proposal was formalized from the ARDOT Commission in
Minute Order No. 2018-049. We were then asked to sponsor and Ordinance to that effect
and, if approved, sign a memorandum of understanding. After considering the pros and
cons, it was decided to place an Ordinance on the City Council Agenda Meeting for
consideration, discussion, and public input. This would allow the public to offer input on
the proposal. At the Agenda Meeting the Council voted to send to the full Council for the
first reading.

Concerns have been expressed by the public and business owners regarding the benefit
of this proposal, particularly long term. These concerns have been discussed with ARDOT
and we are currently awaiting on their response for further discussion and what options
we may have to mitigate this situation.

Until we hear from the ARDOT, we have pulled the Ordinance from the City Council
Meeting Agenda.

Financials
August 2018 financials were discussed. Membership numbers at Veterans Park Community

Programs
Commission asked American Legion Baseball to present first. Cody P. presented for American
Legion Baseball. Has experience with the facilitation of the American Legion Baseball program
in Cabot. They would like to start a Prep- Legion team for 15u in Cabot. It would qualify kids
ages 13-15. No tryouts. Last year yielded 4 teams. Goal is to keep 4 teams with 12 kids per
team. Added revenue would be generated through traveling team’s ability to play on American
Legion CPR fields. Overall goal is to “teach sound fundamentals that lay a solid foundation for
future players to build upon so they may be successful for future baseball endeavors.” 15 u non
high school kid’s cutoff date 9/1. Season to open 3/30- 6/12. State tournament 6/14 with
intentions to host tournament. Every Cabot team would qualify for the state tournament. 9099% of games would be at Cabot American Legion fields and CPR fields. $125 per player.
Sanctioned and ensured through American Legion Baseball. Equipment and uniforms covered
by Legion program. Umpires, gates, and field maintenance would be controlled through CPR.
Junior and Senior programs to 19u have been offered in past. Scholarship opportunities to

47

universities will be offered through Cabot Legion Program and State Legion Program. Cabot has
an impressive ability to sponsor this youth program. William Sheets thanks CPR for their
support of the American Legion program in this area. Commission inquired if this program
works in CPR’s favor. CPR Director Young and CPR Programs Director Mendoza have spoken
with representatives of the program to discuss future partnerships. Considerations of the
program- costs, individuals who do not want to play American Legion, eligible players, and field
space. Commissioner Moudy inquired whether this program would replace existing CPR 13-15
year old division. Yes. Past seasons yielded 4/5 teams in the 13-15 division. Level of competition
will be heightened. CPR and CPR Commission goal is to ensure that every kid has an opportunity
to play. American Legion representatives ensured that every child will have an opportunity to
play. CPR Young drew comparisons to surrounding area American Legion and parks baseball
programs. Further information to be provided at future meetings. CPR would operate 4u to 12u
divisions. Commissioner Whitaker inquired if this would require a legal program agreement.
CPR Director Yes. Commissioner Moudy inquired about current city league fees. $95 per player
including uniform. American Legion is set to have a senior, double AA, and junior team.
American Legion would like to formally communicate with CPR and the Commission to establish
a fair play rule. Current City of Cabot rules apply bat round robin, free substitutions each inning,
and cannot sit two consecutive innings. Commission, CPR Directors, and American Legion to
discuss rules and regulations. Feedback on American Legion field was provided. Facts warranted
rolled ankles, uneven grass positioning, and improved dirt work. Suggestions for improvements
include additional bull pens, rolling and leveling the outfield, and additional sand to fill low
spots. To date completed on American Legion field includes $4000 worth of clay, top dressed
infields, and rebuilt mounds. Richie Road Park fields will continue to be used.
Programs Director Lorenzo Mendoza presented for programs. Fall youth soccer, baseball,
softball, and volleyball have started. Total registration number- 1168 players. Increase of 315
from Fall 2017. Youth basketball registrations started 9/17. Early Bird registrations- 9/17- 10/1.
Registrations will end 10/30. Practices will begin week after Thanksgiving. Pre-season
tournament will begin 2nd week in December. Wrestling registrations are ongoing. New mat has
arrived. Recreational Programmer, Christi Miltz introduction.

excessive number of ants on Crouch Field. The water department has concerns about the
settling of new pipe construction. Half of parking has been blocked off. CPR and school system
worked together to remove and clean up tree area. Thomas Paulson raised a concern regarding
exposed power lines located by shed.

at CPR discretion, they are permitted to park in area. Considerations were made regarding the

Cheer presented. 115 Registered. All, but 1 team was provided cheerleaders. No issues.

None

on official responsibilities, programming, and day to day operations of Veterans Park

James Reed, Planning Commission Chairman

Re:

Hwy 321 & Kerr Station
Development Feasibility

Dear Mr. Reed,
Per the direction of the City Council, I have reviewed the feasibility of development for the
property that was recommended for rezone from Residential to Commercial at the NE
intersection of Hwy 321 & Kerr Station.
DRAINAGE
The subject property lies between The Heights and Hwy 321 on the East side of Kerr Station
Rd. This property has a significant drainage ditch running along the north side which crosses
Hwy 321 on the east side. There is a large Special Flood Hazard Area (Flood Zone) adjacent
to this waterway as well. This special flood hazard area is a Zone AE with base flood
elevations and no regulatory Floodway. The flood zone encompasses much of the north
portion of the subject property; however, a strip approximately 1,000 ft long and 80-135’ wide
exists adjacent to Hwy 321 that is not inundated by the flood zone.
UTILITIES
The subject property has access to a 12” waterline on the north side of Hwy 321 and a 6”
waterline on east side of Kerr Station Road. There is an 8” Sewer line that runs along the
north side of the ditch adjacent to the north boundary of the subject property.
DEVELOPMENT OPTIONS
Residential – A standard residential subdivision is not feasible for this property as it does not
have enough depth to allow an east-west entrance road from Kerr with lots on each side.
Larger lots using the full depth of the property would be possible, but would require 10-12
driveways onto Hwy 321 which does not meet our access management goals.
Commercial/Office – Although commercial development does have its challenges on this site,
it could be done. The most likely development scenario would be an access point onto Kerr
Station Road with another single access driveway onto Hwy 321. Considering a building
depth of 50 feet to minimize impact into the flood zone, this scenario would accommodate 2-4
buildings and 20,000 to 40,000 sf of commercial/office space.

11

CONCERNS AND OTHER CONSIDERATIONS
Some of the concerns brought up by many of the adjoining property owners were tree
removal, buffer, and increased drainage. The staff shares the concerns of the adjoining
owners, but these items are only reviewed when a site plan in brought before the staff
(whether it be a commercial site or a residential plan). The current UDC has provisions for
evaluating drainage and providing buffer requirements. Currently there is nothing stopping
the owner from cutting down all the trees on the property provided it is done within the
guidelines of the USACE and a flood plain development permit.
CONCLUSION
Although this property does have some development obstacles, I believe following the master
land use plan and rezoning the subject property to commercial is the best and highest use of
the property considering the above.
If you have any questions pertaining to the above, please do not hesitate to contact my office.

Sincerely,

that finding in no way affects the validity of the remaining portions of this ordinance.
